titulo: Living the Moment: Talking About Feelings, Personality and Daily Life
titulo_es: Vivir el momento: sentimientos, personalidad y vida diaria
estandares: Expreso gustos, preferencias y emociones con estructuras variadas. Describo situaciones temporales y planes personales, y reflexiono sobre mi carácter y mis experiencias.
competencias: Usar gerundio e infinitivo después de verbos de gusto; ubicar adverbios de frecuencia con precisión; emplear el presente continuo para lo temporal y para planes; describir personalidad y emociones con vocabulario preciso.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: Cada estudiante elabora una autobiografía breve del momento presente: qué disfruta y qué evita, qué está haciendo esta temporada de su vida y qué planes tiene, usando gerundios y presente continuo.
proyecto.descripcion_en: Each student writes a short autobiography of their present moment: what they enjoy and what they avoid, what they are doing in this season of their life and what plans they have, using gerunds and the present continuous.

lecciones.t_en: Likes and dislikes with gerund and infinitive
lecciones.content_es:
Los que siempre piden gerundio

enjoy, avoid, dislike, detest, don't mind, can't stand, keep, practice, finish, suggest:
I enjoy reading. · She avoids eating late. · I can't stand waiting.

Los que aceptan los dos

like, love, hate, prefer, start, begin, continue aceptan gerundio o to + infinitivo casi sin cambio de sentido:
I love dancing = I love to dance.

Matiz: el gerundio suele señalar un gusto general; el infinitivo, una preferencia o una elección puntual.

Los que solo piden infinitivo

want, need, decide, hope, plan, learn, promise, refuse, expect: I want to learn French.

Preferencias comparadas

I prefer swimming to running. · I'd rather swim than run. (would rather va con verbo base, sin to)
lecciones.content_en:
Verbs that always take a gerund

enjoy, avoid, dislike, detest, don't mind, can't stand, keep, practice, finish, suggest:
I enjoy reading. · She avoids eating late. · I can't stand waiting.

Verbs that take both

like, love, hate, prefer, start, begin, continue take either a gerund or to + infinitive with almost no change of meaning:
I love dancing = I love to dance.

Nuance: the gerund usually points to a general taste; the infinitive to a preference or a specific choice.

Verbs that only take the infinitive

want, need, decide, hope, plan, learn, promise, refuse, expect: I want to learn French.

Compared preferences

I prefer swimming to running. · I'd rather swim than run. (would rather takes the base verb, no to)

lecciones.content_es:
Escala y matices

always (100%) · nearly always · usually / normally (80%) · often / frequently (60%) · sometimes (40%) · occasionally (25%) · seldom / rarely / hardly ever (10%) · never (0%).

Reglas de posición

  • Antes del verbo principal: I often feel nervous before exams.
  • Después de to be: She is seldom angry.
  • Entre auxiliar y verbo: He has never apologized.
  • sometimes, usually, occasionally también pueden abrir la oración: Sometimes I feel overwhelmed.

Énfasis

Al inicio de la oración, never, rarely y seldom exigen inversión: Never have I seen something like that. Es una estructura formal y enfática.
lecciones.content_en:
Scale and nuances

always (100%) · nearly always · usually / normally (80%) · often / frequently (60%) · sometimes (40%) · occasionally (25%) · seldom / rarely / hardly ever (10%) · never (0%).

Position rules

  • Before the main verb: I often feel nervous before exams.
  • After to be: She is seldom angry.
  • Between auxiliary and verb: He has never apologized.
  • sometimes, usually, occasionally can also open the sentence: Sometimes I feel overwhelmed.

Emphasis

At the start of a sentence, never, rarely and seldom require inversion: Never have I seen something like that. It is a formal, emphatic structure.

fichas.d_en: Rarely, in a more formal register.

fichas.d_en: Never have I seen…: the auxiliary precedes the subject.

fichas.d_en: She is rarely late, not She rarely is late.

fichas.d: Solo algunos adverbios pueden abrir la oración.
fichas.d_en: Only some adverbs can open the sentence.

lecciones.t: Presente continuo: lo temporal y los planes
lecciones.t_en: Present continuous: temporary situations and plans
lecciones.content_es:
Tres usos que conviene distinguir

  • Ahora mismo: She is talking on the phone.
  • Situación temporal (esta semana, este mes, este año): I'm working on a project this month.
  • Plan futuro ya concretado: We're meeting the counselor on Friday.

Cómo saber cuál es

Las expresiones de tiempo lo definen: right now → ahora; this week/month → temporal; tomorrow, on Friday, next week → plan.

Detalle importante

Para que el continuo sirva como futuro, el plan debe estar acordado: hora, lugar o personas. Si es solo una intención, se prefiere going to; si es una predicción, will.

Verbos de estado

Siguen sin admitir el continuo: I need help now, no I'm needing.
lecciones.content_en:
Three uses worth distinguishing

  • Right now: She is talking on the phone.
  • Temporary situation (this week, this month, this year): I'm working on a project this month.
  • Fixed future plan: We're meeting the counselor on Friday.

How to tell them apart

The time expressions decide: right now → now; this week/month → temporary; tomorrow, on Friday, next week → plan.

Important detail

For the continuous to work as a future, the plan must be arranged: a time, a place or people. If it is only an intention, prefer going to; if it is a prediction, will.

State verbs

They still take no continuous: I need help now, not I'm needing.

lecciones.content_es:
Cómo eres con los demás

empathetic (empático), supportive (que apoya), loyal, tolerant, respectful, sociable, reserved, talkative (hablador), bossy (mandón), jealous (celoso).

Cómo eres contigo y con el trabajo

ambitious, determined (decidido), responsible, organized, creative, curious, perfectionist, impulsive, insecure, self-confident.

Matizar

He's quite shy. · She's a bit stubborn. · He can be rather impatient at times. · She tends to be optimistic.

Falsos amigos

sensible = sensato (sensible en español es sensitive). sympathetic = comprensivo (simpático es nice o friendly).
lecciones.content_en:
How you are with others

empathetic, supportive, loyal, tolerant, respectful, sociable, reserved, talkative, bossy, jealous.

How you are with yourself and your work

ambitious, determined, responsible, organized, creative, curious, perfectionist, impulsive, insecure, self-confident.

Softening

He's quite shy. · She's a bit stubborn. · He can be rather impatient at times. · She tends to be optimistic.

False friends

sensible means having good judgment; sensitive is the one that means easily affected emotionally. sympathetic means understanding, not likeable.

fichas.d_en: Understanding and caring, not likeable.

lecciones.content_es:
Emociones más precisas

overwhelmed (abrumado), frustrated, anxious, grateful (agradecido), relieved (aliviado), hopeful, lonely (solo), motivated, disappointed, embarrassed (avergonzado), guilty (culpable), content (satisfecho).

Estructuras para expresarlas

  • I feel + adjetivo: I feel anxious about the exam.
  • It makes me feel…: Music makes me feel calm.
  • I'm afraid of / worried about / excited about…

Reflexionar sobre uno mismo

I've learned that… · Looking back, I realize… · What I value most is… · One thing I'd like to improve is… · I used to be…, but now I'm…

Falso amigo

embarrassed es avergonzado, no embarazada (que es pregnant).
lecciones.content_en:
More precise emotions

overwhelmed, frustrated, anxious, grateful, relieved, hopeful, lonely, motivated, disappointed, embarrassed, guilty, content.

Structures to express them

  • I feel + adjective: I feel anxious about the exam.
  • It makes me feel…: Music makes me feel calm.
  • I'm afraid of / worried about / excited about…

Reflecting on yourself

I've learned that… · Looking back, I realize… · What I value most is… · One thing I'd like to improve is… · I used to be…, but now I'm…

False friend

embarrassed means ashamed, not expecting a baby (that is pregnant).

lecciones.t: Saludos y comandos en contexto académico
lecciones.t_en: Greetings and commands in an academic context
lecciones.content_es:
Registro académico

Good morning, everyone. · Could I ask a question? · Excuse me, I didn't catch that. · Would you mind repeating? · Thank you for your feedback.

Comandos de trabajo avanzado

Analyze the text. · Summarize the main idea. · Support your answer with evidence. · Compare and contrast the two positions. · Draft an outline. · Peer-review your partner's work. · Cite your sources.

Participar en clase

  • Pedir la palabra: May I add something?
  • Aclarar: What I mean is… · Let me rephrase that.
  • Reconocer: That's a good point. · I hadn't thought of that.

Ojo

Would you mind…? va seguido de gerundio: Would you mind explaining that again?
lecciones.content_en:
Academic register

Good morning, everyone. · Could I ask a question? · Excuse me, I didn't catch that. · Would you mind repeating? · Thank you for your feedback.

Advanced task commands

Analyze the text. · Summarize the main idea. · Support your answer with evidence. · Compare and contrast the two positions. · Draft an outline. · Peer-review your partner's work. · Cite your sources.

Taking part in class

  • Asking for the floor: May I add something?
  • Clarifying: What I mean is… · Let me rephrase that.
  • Acknowledging: That's a good point. · I hadn't thought of that.

Careful

Would you mind…? is followed by a gerund: Would you mind explaining that again?

repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

Para hablar de ti mismo necesitas tres cosas: los patrones verbales (qué verbo pide gerundio y cuál infinitivo), los adverbios de frecuencia bien colocados y el presente continuo para lo temporal y lo planeado.

Puntos gramaticales

  • enjoy, avoid, can't stand + gerundio. want, decide, hope + to.
  • like, love, hate y prefer aceptan los dos.
  • would rather + verbo base; prefer A to B.
  • Never al inicio obliga a invertir: Never have I seen…
  • Continuo para lo temporal (this month) y para citas ya acordadas.

Vocabulario

Adjetivos de personalidad con sus falsos amigos (sensible, sympathetic), emociones precisas (overwhelmed, relieved, embarrassed) y fórmulas académicas de participación.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

To talk about yourself you need three things: verb patterns (which verb takes a gerund and which an infinitive), well-placed frequency adverbs and the present continuous for what is temporary and what is planned.

Grammar points

  • enjoy, avoid, can't stand + gerund. want, decide, hope + to.
  • like, love, hate and prefer take both.
  • would rather + base verb; prefer A to B.
  • Never at the start forces inversion: Never have I seen…
  • Continuous for the temporary (this month) and for arranged appointments.

Vocabulary

Personality adjectives with their false friends (sensible, sympathetic), precise emotions (overwhelmed, relieved, embarrassed) and academic participation formulas.
